scope: Per-CVE residual preconditions reviewed against the refreshed source data and unchanged application/runtime boundary; not a complete native call graph or exploit test.

notes.CVE-2005-2541: GNU tar restores operator snapshots; unsafe archived privilege bits remain an operator/provenance risk. Daemon capability removal does not sandbox privileged restore.
notes.CVE-2007-5686: The advisory concerns OS authentication-log permissions. MakersVault web identity is separate, but this does not waive operator/account-tool exposure.
notes.CVE-2010-4756: Untrusted patterns passed to native glob can exhaust resources. No matching application invocation identified; glibc remains active and indirect calls are not exhaustively excluded.
notes.CVE-2011-3374: The advisory concerns apt-key trust handling. No user-controlled package-manager path identified; operator package/key management remains a separate trust boundary.
notes.CVE-2011-4116: File::Temp remains loadable; temporary-file symlink handling is not excluded by module absence. No application-controlled Perl invocation identified.
notes.CVE-2013-4392: Local symlink manipulation during systemd permission updates remains a tooling/library residual. The API is not a systemd manager; no whole-family absence claim.
notes.CVE-2017-18018: The described chown/chgrp race has recursive dereference preconditions. Startup and restore use ownership tools; protect roots and staging, without claiming all races impossible.
notes.CVE-2018-20796: Crafted native regular expressions can cause recursion/resource exhaustion. No matching application invocation identified; Python regex use does not prove all native regex paths unreachable.
notes.CVE-2019-1010022: The disputed stack-guard bypass concerns exploit mitigations, not missing code. Retain residual impact if another native corruption primitive is available.
notes.CVE-2019-1010023: The described path involves inspecting untrusted ELF with ldd. No uploaded-model-to-ldd path identified; operator execution/inspection remains outside that observation.
notes.CVE-2019-1010024: The disputed address-layout issue concerns cached thread stack/heap mappings. Treat as residual mitigation weakness, not proof of a patched runtime.
notes.CVE-2019-1010025: Predictability of thread heap addresses is disputed upstream. Keep the vendor dispute and possible mitigation weakness distinct from an installed fix.
notes.CVE-2019-9192: The disputed recursion behavior requires a crafted native regex. No matching application invocation identified; retain resource-exhaustion risk rather than excluding glibc.
notes.CVE-2021-45346: Corrupt SQLite databases and crafted queries can expose unintended database bytes. Trusted raw-snapshot provenance is required; read-only access is not parser isolation.
notes.CVE-2022-0563: The described path uses privileged chfn/chsh with Readline configuration. No user-controlled invocation identified; installed account tooling is not categorically excluded.
notes.CVE-2023-31437: The disputed issue affects views of modified sealed journal files. MakersVault's durable application audit is separate; installed system-library/operator risks remain.
notes.CVE-2023-31438: The disputed issue affects detection of truncated/resealed journal files. Do not equate application audit coverage with a systemd journal integrity fix.
notes.CVE-2023-31439: The disputed issue affects integrity checks on modified sealed journal events. No application journal-sealing path identified; no family-wide absence claim.
notes.CVE-2024-56433: Subordinate UID ranges can conflict with locally administered identities. Protect operator UID mappings; default nonzero API identity alone does not prove no collision.
notes.CVE-2025-5278: The affected command is sort with crafted traditional key arguments, not chown. No application-controlled sort argument path identified; utility remains installed.
notes.CVE-2025-60876: BusyBox wget request-target handling can permit HTTP request manipulation. No application URL-to-wget path identified. Fresh CNA bytes are unchanged, but current Alpine backport/fix status remains unverified and needs explicit owner acknowledgment.
notes.CVE-2025-6141: Local termcap parsing can corrupt memory. No application-controlled terminal-tool invocation identified; installed terminal libraries are not proven unreachable through every dependency.
notes.CVE-2025-69720: The described infocmp analysis path can overflow a stack buffer. No application-controlled infocmp invocation identified; retain the scanner High label.
notes.CVE-2025-70873: The SQLite zipfile extension can disclose heap data. Default connection archive functions are absent, but extension/library reachability is not fully excluded.
notes.CVE-2026-15059: The described systemd-oomd IPC path can terminate local processes. No API service-manager path identified; system libraries remain installed.
notes.CVE-2026-15534: Large subjects and specific Perl regex structures can corrupt the heap. Perl core is present; no application-controlled Perl invocation identified, not a size-based safety proof.
notes.CVE-2026-16742: The described escalation requires a homed-managed local user. Web accounts are separate; no whole-systemd exclusion or operator privilege waiver.
notes.CVE-2026-18374: The glibc fopen defect depends on an attacker-controlled encoding-mode extension. No such application mode-string path identified; active libc is not excluded.
notes.CVE-2026-18477: A local writer can influence incremental tar restore through rename races. Private staging alone is insufficient if source/restore paths are attacker-writable; require protected provenance and roots.
notes.CVE-2026-18508: The described hardlink escape involves tar one-top-level extraction and preexisting symlinks. Current restore does not request that option; retain broader privileged archive risks.
notes.CVE-2026-19487: Perl regex prescan can select the wrong match or miss input. No application-controlled Perl filtering path identified; core remains present and unpatched for this ID.
notes.CVE-2026-27171: The described zlib checksum-combine paths can fail to terminate with problematic arguments. No matching caller identified; native decompression usage does not establish absence.
notes.CVE-2026-3184: The described hostname/PAM issue is in OS login with a remote-host option. MakersVault web authentication is separate; local/operator invocations remain residual.
notes.CVE-2026-40228: The described journald forwarding configuration can inject terminal escape sequences. No MakersVault journal-to-terminal path identified; installed system libraries remain.
notes.CVE-2026-42250: The affected tool is bzip2recover, not every compression operation. No application-controlled recovery-tool invocation identified; do not infer a whole-bzip2 fix.
notes.CVE-2026-50813: SQLite SESSION changeset merge/concat paths can disclose data. SESSION remains enabled; no matching application caller identified, not a complete shared-code exclusion.
notes.CVE-2026-53910: The described diff3 defect depends on manipulated diff output. No application-controlled diff3 invocation identified; retain the vendor dispute without calling the utility patched.
notes.CVE-2026-5435: Deprecated DNS-printing helpers can write beyond a supplied buffer. No matching application debug-helper caller identified; retain High severity and active libc residuals.
notes.CVE-2026-54369: Path-based ACL operations can follow attacker-replaced components under privilege. Protect operator roots/staging; ownership tooling and installed libacl are not blanket-excluded.
notes.CVE-2026-54370: Privileged ACL utilities can race pathname replacement. No application-controlled ACL command identified, but operator path control and privilege separation remain required.
notes.CVE-2026-54371: Extended-attribute utilities can follow attacker-substituted path components. No application-controlled attribute-tool invocation identified; protect privileged operator paths.
notes.CVE-2026-54411: The issue requires repeated authentication through pam_userdb plaintext comparison. MakersVault identity is not a PAM service; OS tooling remains present.
notes.CVE-2026-56391: The affected command is uniq with multibyte input and a width option, not chown. No user-controlled invocation identified; retain read/crash residuals.
notes.CVE-2026-56392: The affected command is unexpand with large tab-stop arguments, not chown. No application-controlled invocation identified; retain heap-corruption residuals.
notes.CVE-2026-5704: GNU tar can interpret content differently from pre-extraction inspection, permitting hidden files. Current raw restore invokes tar; trusted origin is essential and checksums are not authentication.
notes.CVE-2026-6238: The affected DNS-printing helpers are distinct from ordinary resolver queries. No matching application helper caller identified; no exhaustive indirect-call exclusion.
notes.CVE-2026-6368: The described wordexp append/free sequence can return invalid memory. No matching application caller identified; installed native code remains a residual.
notes.CVE-2026-6791: Untrusted wordexp tilde expansion can exhaust the native stack. No matching application invocation identified; no assumption that all native input is trusted.
notes.CVE-2026-76642: Failed mount helpers can leave privileged post-mount hooks acting on existing filesystems. No untrusted mount-command path identified; recovery privilege is separate from the daemon.
notes.CVE-2026-78408: Privileged nsenter cgroup joining can leak a powerful descriptor into a target. Do not use operator namespace tooling against untrusted targets under this exception.
notes.CVE-2026-78409: Authorized subdirectory mounts can traverse intermediate symlinks under the described kernel/options. No user-driven mount configuration identified; operator mount roots must remain protected.
notes.CVE-2026-78410: Restricted bind mounts can race writable source paths and alter redirected ownership/mode. No user-driven mount configuration identified; preserve protected operator paths.
